L: Look! There's a smart farm in this subway station.
봐! 이 지하철역에 스마트 팜이 있어.
I said, "There's a smart farm here."
A smart farm? [Can you tell me more about it?]
스마트 팜? 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
A smart farm uses the latest technology to grow vegetables.
스마트 팜은 채소를 재배하기 위해 최신 기술을 사용해.
This song keeps playing in my head.
이 노래가 내 머릿속에서 계속 재생돼.
I didn't get that. [What did you say?]
나 잘 알아듣지 못했어. 뭐라고 말했니?
"An earworm." It's a song that keeps repeating in your mind.
"귀벌레." 그것은 네 마음속에서 계속 반복되는 노래야.
That's interesting. [Can you tell me more about it?]
그거 흥미롭네. 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Most earworms are very easy to remember.
When I feel stressed, I usually watch mukbang.
나는 스트레스 받을 때 보통 먹방을 봐.
I said "mukbang." It's a type of eating show.
Oh, that sounds interesting. [Can you tell me more about it?]
오, 그거 흥미롭게 들려. 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
The host eats a lot of food and communicates with the viewers on the show.
진행자는 쇼에서 많은 음식을 먹고 시청자들과 소통해.
Did you know that the first zipper was used on a shoe?
너는 최초의 지퍼가 신발에 사용되었다는 것을 알았니?
I said, "The first zipper was used on a shoe."
That's interesting. [Can you tell me more about it?]
그거 흥미롭네. 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Sure. A man wanted to put on his shoes quickly, so he made zippers for them.
물론이지. 한 남자가 신발을 빨리 신고 싶어서 신발에 쓸 지퍼를 만들었어.
Yeah. Now, we use zippers on many things like jackets and bags.
응. 이제 우리는 지퍼를 재킷과 가방 같은 많은 것에 사용해.
The race is neck and neck.
I didn't get that. [What did you say?]
나 잘 알아듣지 못했어. 뭐라고 말했니?
[Can you tell me more about it?]
그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
It means something is very close.
그것은 무언가가 매우 대등하다는 것을 의미해.
Wow! Look at the big sculpture over there.
와! 저기에 있는 큰 조각품을 봐.
It's beautiful. The word "love" is in big red letters.
아름다운데. 'love'라는 단어가 큰 빨간 글자로 쓰여 있어.
It's a great example of public art.
I said "public art." It's art for everyone.
"공공 미술"이라고 말했어. 그것은 모두를 위한 미술이야.
I like that idea. [Can you tell me more about it?]
그 아이디어 좋다. 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Sure. It's art in public spaces like parks and streets.
물론이지. 그것은 공원과 거리 같은 공공장소에 있는 미술이야.
Oh, I saw a piece of public art when I visited Jeju-do.
오, 나는 제주도를 방문했을 때 공공 미술 작품 하나를 봤어.
Yeah, they're everywhere. Let's take a photo in front of the sculpture.
그래, 그것들은 어디에나 있어. 그 조각품 앞에서 사진 찍자.
I've never heard of it. [Can you tell me more about it?]
나는 그것에 대해 들어 본 적이 없어. 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Sure. It's the world's largest wall painting. It looks like many books. It's in Incheon.
물론이지. 그것은 세계에서 가장 큰 벽화야. 많은 책처럼 보여. 인천에 있어.
That sounds amazing. Thanks for the information!
What do you need to buy from the market?
Let me check my smart refrigerator.
[Can you tell me more about it?]
그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Sure! It's a refrigerator connected to the internet. I can see inside it from my smartphone.
물론이지! 그것은 인터넷에 연결된 냉장고야. 나는 내 스마트폰으로 그 안을 볼 수 있어.
I just took a great selfie.
[What did you say?] A great what?
[Can you tell me more about it?]
그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Sure! A selfie is a photo you take of yourself.
물론이지! 셀카는 네가 너 자신을 찍은 사진이야.

lines: It was the day of the school play.
Lily practiced for the play for weeks.
The curtains were about to go up, and she felt very nervous.
Her friend smiled and said, “Break a leg!”
Lily said, “Thanks. I will!”
She got on the stage and performed successfully.
Although “Break a leg!” may sound like a bad thing, it actually means “Good luck!”
German actors who came to the United States in the early 20th century first used this phrase.
By wishing each other bad luck, they believed that it would go away.
This expression is still used today.
“Break a leg” is a phrase that people say to wish performers good luck before a show.
Tommy and Lisa were preparing a surprise party for Hana.
But Tommy was not good at keeping secrets.
So, Lisa told him, “Don’t spill the beans.”
Tommy said, “Don’t worry. I promise not to tell Hana.”
Tommy kept his promise and the surprise party was a big success.
Hana was completely surprised.
What does the phrase “spill the beans” mean?
It means to reveal a secret.
Where does this phrase come from?
It comes from an ancient Greek way of voting.
When Greeks voted, they put a white or black bean in a big jar.
When the voting was completed, the beans were spilled to reveal the results.
From then, people began to use this phrase with a new meaning.
Sarah wanted to see a movie with her best friend, Emily.
So, she asked Emily, “Do you want to see a movie with me today?”
Emily replied, “I’m sorry, but I have to take a rain check.
I have to go to my grandmother’s house today.”
“That’s okay. Let’s do it another time,” said Sarah.
Although Sarah was a little disappointed, she understood Emily’s situation.
What does “take a rain check” mean?
It means to refuse an offer politely but wish to do it later.
The phrase “rain check” was first used at a baseball game in the 1880s.
A rain check was a ticket that people got for a future game when a baseball game was canceled because of rain.
Later, rain checks were given at other sporting events.
Over time, “take a rain check” has been widely used to say that you can’t do something now and want to do it later.
